diff_summary: execution-report.js: added ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD to NO_RETRY_REASONS (beside ADVOCATE_DISSENT) and EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH to both NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS (mirroring MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT's membership exactly); added a frozen SEVERITIES constant and an exported failureReasonSeverity(reason) classifier computed from those two sets (non-retriable iff the reason is in NO_RETRY_REASONS or QUARANTINE_REASONS, retriable otherwise, null for a non-string/empty reason); rewired decideLifecycle's 'failed' branch to call failureReasonSeverity(reason) once and branch on it, keeping the QUARANTINE_REASONS.has(reason) check solely to choose between the two existing decision_reason wordings so every returned decision/warn_flag/decision_reason/exit_code stays byte-identical for every reason that existed before this change; exported SEVERITIES and failureReasonSeverity beside the already-exported NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS. SCHEMA_VERSION left at '1.4.0' (parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js hard-asserts the literal); no gate key, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, exitCodeFor, emitted report shape, or existing reason's set membership changed; PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED and STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED were NOT added to either set. references/phase-gates.md: replaced the 'Failure-reason classes' two-prose-bullet-list section with a single 'Failure-reason vocabulary' definition table (Reason | Emitted when | In-run: skips remaining retry budget? | Terminal severity | Source in execution-report.js) covering the whole closed enum plus the two new reasons, each stating its own severity in its own row; added the AC-4 sourcing paragraph naming both the report decision/exit_code and the exported failureReasonSeverity() classifier as the two ways to read severity, and explicitly excluding gates[].detail prose; documented that PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK's non-retriable severity comes from decideLifecycle's unconditional final_status:'quarantined' branch, not from set membership (it is not, and must not become, a member of either set); added an explicit constraint note that PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED/STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED must never be added to either set; added a note distinguishing the attempt-level annotations ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED/CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED (no severity, never terminal) from the closed terminal vocabulary; updated Consensus rule 5's 'uphold' bullet and the operator-directed-repair spent-cap sentence to name ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD explicitly (not {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, not the unresolved ADVOCATE_DISSENT reason); amended gate rule 5 so the default {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE applies only when no more specific vocabulary-table row applies, and named the skills_clean integrity case (EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH) explicitly; updated the Contents entry to match the new section title. references/artifact-layout.md: added a run_manifest.failure_reason prose sentence stating it is null while running and set once, at terminal state, to a value from the closed vocabulary table (cross-referencing phase-gates.md, never restating it), with severity read from that table/classifier and never re-derived from report prose; added a phase_manifest.json prose paragraph distinguishing the ATTEMPT-level failure_reason (which may carry the two no-severity annotations) from run_manifest.failure_reason (always a terminal-vocabulary value with a defined severity); updated the skill_trace 'wrapper is a transcription, never a judgment' paragraph to name the terminal reason (EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, non-retriable, same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT) the job now terminates on instead of the blanket {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE.
implementation_notes: Followed the plan's three-file proposal exactly; no deviations. One design decision the plan left implicit and I had to resolve while writing the phase-gates.md table: PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK (second verify-drift BLOCK) is documented in SKILL.md §4 step 3 as terminating with final_status: 'quarantined' (not 'failed'), and it is NOT a member of NO_RETRY_REASONS or QUARANTINE_REASONS in the code -- its non-retriable severity in practice comes from decideLifecycle's unconditional 'quarantined'-status branch, which quarantines regardless of the reason string, not from the reason-set classification failureReasonSeverity() computes. I verified this empirically: failureReasonSeverity('PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK') returns 'retriable' (it is not in either set), while the row's REAL terminal severity is non-retriable via the status branch. Writing the table naively (severity='non-retriable', source='member of a set') would have been a false claim about set membership that does not exist and would fail a strict failureReasonSeverity(reason)==table.severity join for that one row. Instead the table's Source column for that row states explicitly that its severity comes from the final_status:'quarantined' branch, not from set membership, and the sourcing paragraph calls this out by name so a reader (and any AC-4 drift check) is not misled. I did not add PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK to either code set to make the join trivial, because that would change its verdict for any hypothetical case where it is instead paired with final_status:'failed', which is not authorized by the contract's two named additions and is not needed since its actual documented termination path already goes through the unconditional quarantined-status branch. I also corrected one internal inconsistency while drafting the ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD row: a resolution.action:'repair' that never produces a newer round (phase-gates.md 'Operator-directed repair' step 7) stays blocking under the plain ADVOCATE_DISSENT reason, not ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD, because evalConsensus's gate-detail text reports an unresolved 'repair' as 'unresolved', not 'upheld' -- only an explicit resolution.action:'uphold' produces ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD. The table row states this precisely rather than the looser wording an earlier draft of this note used.
